title: release-provenance --post checks the launcher at X, which a Release run no longer publishes, and the promote-published X launcher carries no provenance
description: Found by the LCLI-616/618 reviewer (2026-09-27), outside that diff; confirmed here by reading scripts/release-provenance.mjs runPost at dev bb8b2662. Since LCLI-621 (ODOC-302), a Release run stages the root launcher as X-rc.N, and the launcher at X reaches npm only later, when scripts/promote-latest.mjs fresh-publishes it --tag latest. release.yml's provenance-post job runs release-provenance.mjs --post, which checks releasePackages() (the launcher plus six platforms) at X. So in a publish:true run it (a) queries @opum-ai/lore@X, which does not exist yet, and (b) never checks the rc launcher the run actually published. It fails only on a dangling commit, so the run does not go red; it just checks the wrong object. Separately and larger: promote-latest publishes the X launcher from the operator's machine with a token, not through OIDC trusted publishing, so the launcher on latest never carries provenance even once LCLI-482 is fixed. The platforms keep whatever provenance their staging publish had. Whether the launcher's final publish should move into CI, to get provenance, is a design question for opum-agent (it touches Article 3.5's promote step and quest-cli's mirror, QCLI-399), not a local fix.

acceptanceCriteria.text: provenance-post (release-provenance.mjs --post) checks the packages a Release run actually published: six platforms at X and the launcher at X-rc.N, never the launcher at X; a test pins the package/version set

The provenance of the X launcher published by promote-latest.mjs is decided by opum-agent (CI publish with OIDC, or an accepted no-provenance launcher documented as such), and the runbook states which; the ruling is recorded on this task
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the release.yml / scripts change
